criteria-adhd.title: ADHD
criteria-adhd.oneLine: A lasting pattern of poor attention, overactivity or impulsivity, from childhood, seen in more than one place, that holds the person back.

facts.label: Threshold
facts.value: 6 or more in either symptom group (5 or more from age 17)

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 6 months or more

facts.label: Onset
facts.value: Several symptoms before age 12

facts.label: Settings
facts.value: 2 or more settings (home, school, work, friends)

facts.label: Impairment
facts.value: Clearly gets in the way of school, work or social life

sections.title: Core picture
bullets: Two symptom groups: inattention, and hyperactivity with impulsivity
Symptoms are more than expected for the child's age and stage
Seen in more than one place, not only at home or only in class
Adults often show restlessness inside and disorganised life, not running about

sections.title: Inattention (9 possible signs)
bullets: Careless mistakes, loses track of tasks
Seems not to listen, drifts off mid-conversation
Avoids long mental effort, loses things, forgetful daily

sections.title: Hyperactivity and impulsivity (9 possible signs)
bullets: Fidgets, leaves the seat, runs or climbs when not suitable
Talks a lot, blurts out answers
Cannot wait a turn, interrupts others

pairs.label: Combined
pairs.value: Both groups reach the threshold over the last 6 months

pairs.label: Mainly inattentive
pairs.value: Inattention reaches it, hyperactivity and impulsivity do not

pairs.label: Mainly hyperactive and impulsive
pairs.value: Hyperactivity and impulsivity reach it, inattention does not

sections.title: Specifiers
bullets: In partial remission: full threshold met before, fewer symptoms now but still impairing

sections.title: Severity
bullets: Mild: few symptoms beyond the threshold, minor impairment
Moderate: in between
Severe: many symptoms, or marked impairment

sections.title: Rule out
bullets: Not only during a psychotic illness
Not better explained by anxiety, mood, dissociative, personality or substance problems
Check sleep, hearing, vision, thyroid and absence seizures first
Rule out a learning disorder, or find it as well: they often come together

pairs.label: Specific learning disorder
pairs.value: Trouble mainly in one skill (reading, writing, maths); attention is fine elsewhere

pairs.label: Anxiety
pairs.value: Restless and distracted by worry; settles when the worry settles

pairs.label: Bipolar disorder
pairs.value: Clear episodes with a change from usual self, not a lifelong steady pattern

pairs.label: Autism
pairs.value: Social communication differences and fixed routines are the core

pairs.label: Oppositional defiant disorder
pairs.value: Refuses on purpose and argues; ADHD forgets or cannot keep at it

pairs.label: Trauma or home stress
pairs.value: Started after a stressor; hypervigilance rather than true inattention

sections.title: First-line care
bullets: Under 5: parent training first; medicine only on specialist advice
School age: advice to parents and school, classroom changes, then medicine if still impairing
Methylphenidate is the usual first medicine; atomoxetine is an option
Adults: medicine is usually offered first, with support and coaching
Check height, weight, pulse and blood pressure before and during medicine

sections.title: In the Indian clinic
bullets: Parents may say 'bahut shararti hai' (very naughty) or 'dhyan nahi deta' (doesn't pay attention)
Get a teacher's report as well as the parents'; it is the second setting
Large classes and rote learning can hide or exaggerate symptoms: ask about home too
Under the RPWD Act 2016, specific learning disabilities count; ADHD itself is not listed

alert.title: Common mistakes
points: Labelling a bright but bored or sleepy child
Calling it ADHD when symptoms appear only at home or only in one class
Missing ADHD in girls: often the quiet, inattentive presentation
Forgetting adults: the onset is in childhood but help may first be sought at 30

criteria-mdd.title: Major depressive disorder
criteria-mdd.oneLine: Two weeks or more of low mood or lost interest, with body and thinking changes, clearly different from the usual self.

facts.label: Threshold
facts.value: 5 or more of 9 symptoms; one must be low mood or loss of interest

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: Most of the day, nearly every day, for 2 weeks or more

facts.label: Impairment
facts.value: Clear distress, or trouble at work, home or with people

sections.title: Core picture
bullets: A change from how the person usually is
Low, empty or hopeless mood (in young people it can look irritable)
Loss of interest or pleasure in almost everything

sections.title: Body
bullets: Sleep too little or too much
Appetite or weight change (more than 5 percent in a month counts)
Tired, slowed down, or restless

sections.title: Thinking
bullets: Feeling worthless or too guilty
Poor concentration, hard to decide
Thoughts of death or suicide

sections.title: Specifiers
bullets: Single episode or recurrent (2 months or more well between episodes)
With anxious distress
With mixed features
With melancholic or atypical features
With psychotic features (mood-congruent or not)
With catatonia
With peripartum onset (in pregnancy or within 4 weeks after birth); with seasonal pattern

sections.title: Severity
bullets: Mild, moderate or severe, by how many symptoms, how intense and how much they impair
In partial or full remission

sections.title: Rule out
bullets: Not caused by a substance, a medicine or a medical illness
Never a manic or hypomanic episode (that makes it bipolar)
Not better explained by a psychotic disorder

pairs.label: Bipolar depression
pairs.value: Any past mania or hypomania: always ask before starting an antidepressant

pairs.label: Normal grief
pairs.value: Waves of pain tied to the loss; self-worth stays intact

pairs.label: Persistent depressive disorder
pairs.value: Milder or same, but 2 years or more

pairs.label: Hypothyroidism, anaemia, medicines
pairs.value: Check thyroid, blood count, and drugs such as steroids

pairs.label: Adjustment disorder
pairs.value: Tied to a stressor and does not reach the 5 of 9 threshold

pairs.label: Substance use
pairs.value: Alcohol and cannabis both lower mood; ask about every substance

sections.title: First-line care
bullets: Less severe: guided self-help, group CBT or behavioural activation, or exercise
More severe: individual CBT or behavioural activation, an antidepressant, or both together
An SSRI such as sertraline or escitalopram is the usual first medicine
Psychotic depression: antidepressant with an antipsychotic; ECT for severe or life-threatening cases

sections.title: In the Indian clinic
bullets: Often presents as body complaints: 'pura sharir dard karta hai', weakness, 'ghabrahat'
Ask about mood directly after the body complaints are heard
Tele MANAS (14416) is the free national mental health line

alert.title: Common mistakes
points: Thinking a clear reason (job loss, illness) means it is not depression
Not asking about suicide directly: asking does not put the idea in the head

pharm-lithium.title: Lithium: levels, toxicity and monitoring
pharm-lithium.oneLine: A narrow safe window: check the level 12 hours after the last dose, and know what pushes it up.

facts.label: Usual target
facts.value: 0.6 to 0.8 mmol/L

facts.label: Some people
facts.value: 0.8 to 1.0 mmol/L (mania, or relapse at lower levels)

facts.label: Older adults
facts.value: Often lower targets

facts.label: When to take blood
facts.value: 12 hours after the last dose

facts.label: Toxicity likely
facts.value: From about 1.5 mmol/L, can happen lower

head: Cause
Why
rows: Less water and salt, kidneys keep more lithium
Kidneys hold on to lithium with sodium
Less lithium cleared by the kidneys
BP medicines: ACE inhibitors, ARBs, thiazide diuretics

head: Stage
Signs
rows: Fits, drowsiness to coma, kidney failure

sections.title: Monitoring
bullets: Before starting: kidney function, thyroid, calcium, weight; ECG if heart risk; pregnancy test if relevant
Level weekly after starting and after each dose change, until stable
Then every 3 months in the first year, then usually every 6 months
Kidney function and thyroid every 6 months; calcium and weight regularly
Stop gradually, over at least 4 weeks, to lower the risk of relapse

sections.title: Interactions
bullets: Ask before any new painkiller or BP tablet
Teach: drink enough water in summer, and if vomiting or diarrhoea, call the clinic

sections.title: Common side effects
bullets: Thirst and passing a lot of urine
Fine tremor, weight gain
Underactive thyroid; raised calcium
Lowers suicide risk in mood disorders

alert.title: Emergencies
points: Lithium toxicity: Coarse tremor, vomiting, unsteady, confused. Stop lithium, urgent level and kidney tests, medical care.

facts.value: Count the months first, then ask: is it only during mood episodes, and is it only a delusion?

head: Brief psychotic
Schizophreniform
Schizophrenia
Schizoaffective
Delusional
rows: Mood episodes for most of the illness
1 or more: delusions, hallucinations, disorganised speech or behaviour
Schizophrenia symptoms with a major mood episode
Psychosis 2 weeks or more with no mood episode
Hallucinations, if any, small and on theme
Mostly kept, apart from the belief

facts.value: Low mood

pairs.label: Major depressive disorder
pairs.value: For: 2 weeks or more, 5 of 9, clear change. Against: Past mania; clear medical cause.

pairs.label: Bipolar depression
pairs.value: For: Past high spells, family history, young onset. Against: No highs ever, confirmed by family.

pairs.label: Persistent depressive disorder
pairs.value: For: Low most days for 2 years or more. Against: Clear start weeks ago.

pairs.label: Grief
pairs.value: For: Waves tied to the loss, self-worth kept. Against: Worthlessness, steady emptiness.

pairs.label: Adjustment disorder
pairs.value: For: Started within 3 months of a stressor, below threshold. Against: Full depressive picture.

pairs.label: Substance or medicine
pairs.value: For: Started with alcohol, steroids, isotretinoin, beta blockers. Against: Lasts weeks after stopping.

pairs.label: Medical illness
pairs.value: For: Thyroid, anaemia, B12, diabetes, stroke, Parkinson's. Against: Normal tests and examination.

therapy-cbt.title: CBT: the model, thinking errors and a session
therapy-cbt.oneLine: How we think about a situation shapes how we feel and act; change the thought or the action and the feeling follows.

facts.label: The model
facts.value: Situation, then an automatic thought, then feeling, body and behaviour; the behaviour often keeps the thought going.

facts.label: Sessions
facts.value: Usually 50 minutes, weekly; often 12 to 20 sessions for depression

sections.title: Used for
bullets: Depression and anxiety disorders
OCD (with exposure), PTSD (trauma-focused), eating disorders (adapted)
Insomnia (CBT-I), psychosis (CBTp)

sections.title: Steps
steps: Each session: mood check, agenda, homework review, main work, new homework, feedback
Assess and agree goals; draw the person's own cycle (formulation)
Teach the model with their example
Catch automatic thoughts; test them against evidence
Find the deeper rules and core beliefs behind the thoughts

pairs.label: Thought record
pairs.value: Situation, thought, feeling, evidence for and against, a balanced thought

pairs.label: Socratic questions
pairs.value: Guided questions so the person finds the answer

pairs.label: Behavioural activation
pairs.value: Plan small rewarding and needed activities, despite low mood

pairs.label: Behavioural experiment
pairs.value: Test a prediction in real life

pairs.label: Problem solving
pairs.value: Define, list options, choose, try, review

head: Error
Sounds like
rows: 'If it is not perfect, it is a failure'
'I feel guilty, so I must have done wrong'

sections.title: How it sounds
bullets: What went through your mind just then?
What is the evidence for that thought? And against?
What would you tell a friend who thought that?

points: Acute psychosis or severe mania (stabilise first)
Someone too unwell to concentrate: start with behaviour

theory-learning.title: Learning theories and attachment
theory-learning.oneLine: We learn by pairing (classical), by consequences (operant) and by watching (social learning); early bonds shape attachment.

facts.label: Who
facts.value: Ivan Pavlov, B. F. Skinner, Albert Bandura, John Bowlby, Mary Ainsworth

facts.label: Core idea
facts.value: Behaviour, including fear and habits, is learned and can be unlearned.

head: Classical (Pavlov)
Operant (Skinner)
rows: A link between an act and its result
Bell, then food: the bell alone brings saliva
Pressing a lever brings food: pressing increases
Unconditioned and conditioned stimulus and response
Extinction: bell without food; may return later (spontaneous recovery)

head: Add something
Take something away
rows: Negative reinforcement (headache stops after a tablet)

head: Schedule
Reward comes
Pattern
rows: After a set number of acts
Fast, with a pause after each reward

head: Style
When the carer leaves and returns
rows: Upset when left, comforted on return
Little upset, ignores the carer on return
Very upset, clings and resists on return
Confused, frozen or contradictory; linked to frightening care

pairs.label: Generalisation
pairs.value: Responding to stimuli like the learned one

pairs.label: Shaping
pairs.value: Rewarding steps closer to the target behaviour

pairs.label: Modelling
pairs.value: Learning by watching (Bandura's Bobo doll study)

pairs.label: Self-efficacy
pairs.value: Belief one can do it; drives effort (Bandura)

sections.title: In the clinic
bullets: Phobias can be learned by pairing; exposure is the unlearning
Avoidance is negative reinforcement: relief keeps it going
Token economies and behaviour charts use operant ideas

sections.title: Limits
bullets: Ignores thinking and biology on its own; CBT adds thoughts
Attachment styles describe infants; adult styles are measured differently

deeper.label: Exposure and response prevention, and graded exposure
Development in tables: Freud, Erikson, Piaget, Kohlberg
